title: Benchmark reproducibility self-audit: does the SDK's Run B win survive an embedding swap?
summary: Re-run BENCHMARKS.md's Run B 'with-SDK beats flat-context' comparison with `--embedding-provider` swapped and retrieval depth held constant, applying the exact critique the LightMem reproduction (arXiv 2607.29104) and MemPalace audit (arXiv 2604.21284) used to debunk other vendors' claimed wins.
description:
Two new findings in the August 2026 competitive-analysis update directly attack the credibility of vendor-reported memory-system benchmark gains: 'Reproducing LightMem: Naive RAG Is Just as Good for Memory Management' (Zhou et al., arXiv 2607.29104, July 31 2026) found retriever/embedding choice alone swings accuracy 58.1%→75.5%, and that naive raw-turn RAG matches or beats LightMem's constructed memories at equal retrieval depth; the earlier MemPalace audit (arXiv 2604.21284) found a headline 96.6% Recall@5 was mostly attributable to the default embedding model, not the claimed 'spatial palace' architecture. This SDK's own BENCHMARKS.md Run B currently reports the with-SDK path scoring *below* flat-context overall (84.0% vs 94.0%) but Run D (after BENCH-3a/3b/3c's Consolidator+Reconciler wiring) reports the SDK closing or reversing that gap — a claimed win that, per the same critique, should be checked against embedding choice before being treated as architecture-driven.

Re-run Run D's exact configuration via `scripts/run_benchmarks.py --suite retrieval` with `--embedding-provider` swapped to a different provider than the one Run D used (nomic-embed-text), holding `--top-k`, `--seed 42`, and the Consolidator/Reconciler flags identical, and record the resulting category breakdown as a new 'Run E — embedding-swap reproducibility check' section in BENCHMARKS.md, directly comparable to Run D's table. If the SDK's win holds within a small margin across embedding providers, state that explicitly as evidence the gain is architecture-driven, not embedding-driven — the strongest form of the claim. If it doesn't hold, correct BENCHMARKS.md's summary-across-runs section to say so, following this project's own established discipline (BENCH-1 through BENCH-5 already root-caused and re-measured rather than just asserting improvement) applied here to a claimed win instead of a gap. Independent of TRU-1/TRU-2/TRU-3/TRU-5.
